title: Toward Systematic Counterfactual Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models: The CAFFE Framework
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured counterfactual fairness by detecting semantic disparities and biased behavior in LLM responses when prompts were varied with sensitive attributes, including those related to religion. This involved identifying stereotypes in religious contexts.
findings: All tested models (GPT-4o mini, LLaMA-2-7B-CHAT, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2) exhibited high fairness violation rates (Attack Success Rate - ASR) for the religion bias category, especially under the Question Answering (Q&A) intent, indicating recurring issues and persistent fairness vulnerabilities in this dimension.
